articles.title: Patch Tuesday, May 2026 Edition
articles.summary: CISA, the agency supposed to protect America's cyber infrastructure, leaked their own AWS GovCloud keys on GitHub like amateur hour. The irony is so thick you could encrypt it with their exposed credentials.

articles.title: Microsoft shuts down illegal code-signing operation used by ransomware crims to mask their malware
articles.summary: London's finest made over 700,000 data requests to Big Tech last year, because apparently knocking on doors is so 20th century. FOIA strikes again, exposing the surveillance state's impressive appetite for your digital breadcrumbs.

articles.title: Clear your calendar, Drupal user: You have a critically urgent patch to install
articles.summary: CISA strikes again with a GitHub repo containing files literally named 'external-secret-repo-creds.yaml' and 'AWS-Workspace-Firefox-Passwords.csv'. It's like they wanted to get pwned with that level of OPSEC fail.

articles.title: Typosquatting Is No Longer a User Problem. It's a Supply Chain Problem
articles.summary: GitHub got breached via compromised employee device, with TeamPCP exfiltrating 3,800+ internal repos. When the house of code gets its own code stolen, that's some next-level supply chain irony right there.

articles.title: Zscaler Partners with Global System Integrators to Launch Project AI-Guardian to Help Accelerate Enterprise AI Adoption
articles.summary: Microsoft scrambles to patch YellowKey, a BitLocker bypass that makes disk encryption about as useful as a chocolate teapot. CVE-2026-45585 proves that even crypto can't save you from Microsoft's creative interpretation of security.

articles.title: Crook leaks 468k+ records, claims they pwned Portugal’s postal carrier
articles.summary: Project Glasswing expands responsible disclosure beyond their walled garden, finally letting security researchers share findings with the world. About time the defender pool got deeper than a kiddie pool.

articles.title: Grafana Labs refuses ransom after hackers steal already-open-source code
articles.summary: TeamPCP's supply chain rampage hits peak chaos with a compromised Checkmarx Jenkins plugin and self-spreading Mini Shai-Hulud worm. When your malware references Dune, you know the attackers have culture.

articles.title: Grafana says hackers hit its GitHub environment, demand ransom to prevent codebase release — but it's refusing to pay
articles.summary: Grafana Labs gets extorted over already-open-source code and tells hackers to pound sand. Sometimes the best defense against ransomware is just laughing at the absurdity of it all.

articles.title: Key findings from the Verizon DBIR 2026: Slower vulnerability remediation meets faster exploitation
articles.summary: Multiple US healthcare breaches hit millions because apparently patient privacy is just a suggestion. The HHS tracker keeps growing like a digital morgue of medical data disasters.

articles.title: ABB CoreSense HM and CoreSense M10
articles.summary: Verizon's 2026 DBIR reveals vuln exploitation is now the #1 attack vector while patching gets slower. It's like watching a slow-motion car crash where the brakes are made of bureaucracy.
